analysis.title: Global Reflections - Louis Miller - 23 Oct 2026
key_insights: Goldman Prime Book desk says the market is in a hedge fund deleveraging episode. About 90% of Prime book GMV is quants and multi-managers, so short-term stops matter more than medium-term value.
The AI complex is in a drawdown. The AI vs AI At Risk Pair (GSPUARTI) is down double digits year to date, and the S&P ex AI (SPXXAI) has overtaken the S&P 500 on YTD returns.
Desk view is to buy the dip and selectively reposition into AI, starting with Power, Hyperscalers, Inference and Cyber. It separates scepticism and uncertainty from overvaluation.
Beta-adjusted nets fell 3.5 pts on the week and 10.3 pts on the month. The level is a 1-year low, the 14th percentile on a 3-year lookback and the 33rd percentile on a 5-year lookback.

META results and Prime Book color show the market is focused on AI financing, return on capital and positioning. Hedge funds have de-grossed in 7 of the last 8 sessions at an accelerating pace. Infotech saw long selling and short adds, and net allocation to Semis and Semicap Equipment is the lowest this year.

The desk prefers Power (GSX1POW1), as midterm concerns fade, and broader datacentre equipment (GSTMTDAT). It sees the latter as the clear beneficiary of hyperscaler capex, with earnings showing no sign of slowing while price performance has faded since summer.

Healthcare is an AI-uncorrelated pocket benefiting from AI use (GSHLCAIP, recently rebalanced). The beneficiaries are AI-enabled diagnostics and precision medicine, AI infrastructure and picks-and-shovels, AI-driven drug discovery and clinical development, and operational productivity.

The High Beta Momentum Pair (GSPRHIMO) has erased all YTD gains after a 43% drawdown from its roughly 70% June peak. It is re-testing July lows, and META's earnings reinforced the costs-vs-returns debate.
GSTMTAIP (AI Beneficiaries) had its worst day versus SPXXAI since DeepSeek Monday. SPXXAI has closed the gap with SPX, which is up 6.5% in October.

The desk calls buying the momentum dip a more attractive risk/reward. Positioning is the cleanest since June 2025 but still at the 73rd percentile, drawdown is elevated versus history, and earnings of the winners have risen steadily.

Cyclical headwinds remain: slowing growth, higher oil prices, tighter financial conditions and a tightening cycle. The desk would use GSXUCYCL as a funding short alongside its Low Quality expressions (NPTC, LOWQ, DEBT).

UK Consumer Confidence had its largest ex-Covid decline since Brexit on cost of living concerns. The UK Consumer basket (GSXEUKCO) is up 10% over the last month on a momentum unwind and trades at 13x PE, above the 90th percentile of its 3-year history.
The desk expects potential tax increases at next week's Autumn Budget, a widely expected BoE hike in November and weak 3Q reporting to reverse the recent squeeze in GSXEUKCO.

On China, stronger-than-expected data has not offset worries about domestic demand and the AI unwind. Friday's rebound in Chinese equities came from national-team-linked ETF buying, which suggests policy support remains active. Investors still will not deploy risk meaningfully without a more durable catalyst.
The desk continues to prefer high dividend defensives in China (GSXACHHN) over AI growth (GSXACART).
Hyperscaler (GSXUHYPR) earnings expectations have not been revised since July.

The Power Up America basket (GSENEPOW) was rebalanced to reflect growing behind-the-meter forecasts. It cut overall utilities weights while keeping leading IPPs higher, excluded exploration and production, and added weight to alternatives and behind-the-meter/on-campus generation. The desk expects the group to benefit from infrastructure spending beyond the hyperscaler capex cycle.
